items.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Buster came and played the bass... Higgins said that we should do something together... make a separate arrangement and come in and play with them.

ctx.x: Higgins was the most compassionate being, and all these cats was always askin’ him for bread and stuff, you know, and “Aww, I need a transmission on my car...” “I need this”, and he was a selfless man. He’d just get people whatever they wanted. And he was selfless and he... you know. I remember... Higgins and I were close, man. See, because that record, Acoustic Masters that we made - it was around early ‘90s, someone called and wanted me to do a project, and I said, Higgins, Ron Carter, and Cedar. Course I knew…

that we should do something together. Anyway, Cedar was going into Catalinas and so they called and asked me would I make a separate arrangement and come in and play with them. But Higgins and I always had this beautiful chemistry.
